meeting_summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, expected concurrency, streaming needs, and token/sec benchmarking to compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer concerned about 99th/95th latency for short prompts and streaming interactivity for their chat product; wants hands-on benchmark and security docs before pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
security: SOC2 / VPC / KMS / audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Myers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Good thanks, bit of a busy day but excited.
[00:11] Marcus Wu: Hi, Marcus here. We're the ML team lead, so I'll drive the latency/workload questions.
[00:18] Jordan Myers: Great. Quick agenda: get your current targets, constraints, then we can talk Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and plan a benchmark run.
[00:28] Ravi Patel: Sounds good. We're mainly worried about p95 for our chat assistant, targets are roughly 150ms p95 for short completions (~30 tokens) and under 500ms p95 at 4 concurrent users per server for longer flows.
[00:42] Priya Nair: Ok that's helpful. Is that 150ms end-to-end or just model?
[00:47] Marcus Wu: End-to-end, user to rendered token, roughly. We also stream tokens to the UI.
[00:53] Jordan Myers: Got it. So streaming matters. Do you currently do token-by-token flush or chunked streaming?
[00:58] Marcus Wu: Token-by-token in prod for best UX, but if throughput demands it we can do small chunking.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Great. A couple clarifying Qs: what's your concurrency pattern - is it many users with short bursts or long sessions with more tokens?
[01:12] Marcus Wu: Mix; the busiest flows are short bursts from search-like queries, a median of 35 tokens, tail up to 800 tokens per session for multi-step assistant dialogs.
[01:21] Lena Ortiz: We run in multiple regions - US & EU - data residency is important for EU customers.
[01:26] Jordan Myers: Noted. For p95 150ms for ~30 tokens, on Hosted we typically recommend a small model variant with low-latency kernels and streaming tuned. But p95 150ms is aggressive. Can you share current measured model latencies?
[01:40] Marcus Wu: Today's stack is mostly quantized gpt-small variants on OEM infra, p95 model-only is around 80-90ms but end-to-end is 180-220ms - network & rendering add.
[01:52] Priya Nair: Ok that's useful. With Redwood Dedicated you get pinned capacity that reduces variance; with our serving runtime and KV cache plus batching controls we can often shave 20-40% off model-side p95 for similar throughput.
[02:06] Ravi Patel: Do you have numbers for token/sec throughput at different instance types? We have a throughput goal of 1.5k tokens/sec per app instance at peak.
[02:15] Priya Nair: We do. Roughly, on our Dedicated 8xA10 config we see sustained token/sec of ~2k for medium-length sequences with batching, but it depends on sequence length and quantization. We'll share the spreadsheet with run artifacts.
[02:27] Marcus Wu: How do you handle concurrent KV cache across multiple requests? We see a lot of repeated prefixes.
[02:33] Priya Nair: We have prefix caching at the request router; if you can point to common prefixes we can reduce repeated compute and that improves effective token/sec and latency for repeated contexts. But caching benefits depend on distribution - so sample prompts help.
[02:45] Jordan Myers: For the Hosted plan we have autoscaling which helps but p95 can vary with noisy neighbors; Dedicated removes that variable and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control plus KMS integration. What's your priority: predictable p95 or cost minimization?
[02:59] Lena Ortiz: Predictability first, cost second. We're willing to start on Dedicated to get SLOs.
[03:06] Marcus Wu: Also question on streaming: does Redwood stream token-by-token or micro-batch? We need low jitter.
[03:12] Priya Nair: We can do token-by-token streaming with low jitter; our runtime flush interval is configurable and we can tune to your UX. Micro-batching reduces cost but adds latency/jitter.
[03:22] Ravi Patel: For security, we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), VPC peering, and KMS. Any enterprise customers with Private install?
[03:31] Jordan Myers: Yes, multiple. We support SAML SSO, RBAC, VPC peering, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private. We'll attach SOC2 and a network diagram.
[03:39] Marcus Wu: For benchmarking, we want a 2-hour run that simulates our traffic distribution - short bursts, token-by-token streaming, and a tail of long sessions. Can you do that?
[03:49] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll bring a benchmark harness (we usually use loader clients that emulate token-level streaming) and run it against Hosted and Dedicated variants so you get comparative numbers.
[03:59] Jordan Myers: Can you send us your sample prompt set and token histogram? That helps tune batch sizes and cache.
[04:04] Marcus Wu: I'll share a week of anonymized logs.
[04:07] Lena Ortiz: Timeline: want pilot next quarter, decision by end of Q1.
[04:11] Jordan Myers: Sounds doable. We'll propose a Dedicated pilot cost and a comparison to Hosted per-token pricing.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: Anything else on observability - can we get per-route p95 dashboards and per-token cost breakdown?
[04:23] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, latency breakdown, and you'll get traces for slow requests. We can enable retention on a trial.
[04:31] Marcus Wu: One more thing - how do fallbacks work if a pinned instance is unhealthy? We need automatic fallback to an alternate region or model shard.
[04:39] Jordan Myers: We have smart routing and automatic fallback policies; can route by latency or region and fail over to a compatible model variant. We'll document the canary and rollback policy.
[04:47] Lena Ortiz: Ok, recap and next steps?
[04:51] Jordan Myers: Recap: SableTech wants predictability for p95 ~150ms short completions, streaming token-by-token, concurrency patterns described, and dedicated pilot is preferred. Next steps: Jordan send perf spreadsheet and pricing, Priya schedule benchmark, Marcus share prompts and token histogram, we'll run hosted vs dedicated bench, and share SOC2/VPC/KMS docs.
[05:13] Marcus Wu: Thanks all.
[05:15] Ravi Patel: Thanks.
[05:17] Jordan Myers: Thanks - we'll follow up in email.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: Bye.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and truncated words typical of call-transcripts.
